land.text: the Sulu archipelago, which the sultan and his datus submitted to Spain in the capitulation signed at Jolo on 22 July 1878 ('Bases of Peace and Capitulation')

successors.note: The infobox shows a Spanish protectorate 1851-1899 and annexation to the United States on 22 March 1915; the Sulu page says the sultanate 'effectively ceased' then. Cliopatria's Sulu row runs to 1879.

capitals.name: Buansa (Jolo island)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Buansa (1457-1878)'; Maimbung (1878-1893) and Palawan (1893-1915) follow the end of this dossier. Coordinates are Jolo island, approximate: no place named Buansa is in the gazetteer.

correction.text: Sharif ul-Hashim settled in Buansa on Jolo island: the Sulu islands round Jolo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: infobox 'Established c. 1457'; Cliopatria starts in 1459. The page also gives 17 November 1405 as an alternative founding date and the Philippine NHCP 'around 1450'.

correction.text: Jolo island and the Sulu islands, the seat Buansa

keyframe_review.note: 1,778 km2 (121.76-122.29 E, 6.39-6.78 N): the cells are exactly Basilan's four, not Jolo (Buansa, 121.0 E). The page gives no area and describes only the peak extent; the early core is the Sulu islands round Buansa. Infobox: 'Bruneian vassal (1457-1578)', a status the Brunei dossier carries.

correction.text: as 1459: Jolo and the Sulu islands; Cliopatria has no row for 1507-1528

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the gap 1507-1528 in the Cliopatria row. The sultanate existed throughout (infobox 1457-1915); the page dates no change of land in these years.

3,845 km2: Sulu province, Tawi-Tawi and Basilan, the 'islands that bordered the western peninsula of Zamboanga' (Sulu page); page gives no area. Unverified for its years beyond that line; the page dates the end of Bruneian vassalage to 1578 and the Spanish landing at Jolo to 1637 (Spanish-Moro conflict page). The ledger adds the archipelago's outer islands in 1529 at confidence 1.

union.text: Palawan, which Sulu 'gave up to Spain in 1705'

correction.text: the archipelago and Palawan, with North Borneo added only in 1704 ('as a prize for helping the Sultan of Brunei')

keyframe_review.note: 48,038 km2: the archipelago plus the east and north of Sabah (149 of Sabah's 282 cells). The North Borneo dispute page puts the receipt of north-eastern Borneo in 1704; the Bruneian Civil War of 1660 page (1661-1673) says Sulu claims eastern Sabah as the reward for helping Muhyiddin but gives no year and calls it 'not clear to historians'. Cliopatria's 1673 date follows the war; the ledger uses 1704. Palawan is not in any Cliopatria shape but the Sulu page says it was given up in 1705, so it is added here from 1673 (when it was first held is not on the page).

correction.text: the 1673-1747 realm with North Borneo, without the area of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bulungan

keyframe_review.note: 68,286 km2 = the 1673 shape plus exactly the 79 cells of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bulungan (1734-1747, which stops the year before): Cliopatria folds Bulungan into Sulu. The Bulungan page says Bulungan was Berau's vassal from 1731 and 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Sulu (1789-1855)'; before 1789 the land is not Sulu's, and after 1789 it is a vassal tint (ledger vassal_start 1789), not direct land.

correction.text: as 1748: without the Bulungan area; Basilan leaves with the 1762 cession (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 68,171 km2, the same cells as 1748. Bulungan is a vassal 1789-1855 only. The Sulu page says Sulu ceded Basilan to Spain in 1762 (the ledger event); the Spanish-Moro page puts a cession of Basilan in the peace treaty of 1724 instead.

correction.text: without the Bulungan area (a vassal 1789-1855) and without Basilan (ceded to Spain 1762)

keyframe_review.note: 67,910 km2: Cliopatria drops two southern cells (about 2.8-2.95 N) from the 1752 shape in 1830 and keeps Basilan; the pages opened date neither. Bulungan was Sulu's vassal until it 'stopped paying tribute to Sulu for 50 years' in 1855.

correction.text: the archipelago and North Borneo as of 1877, shown only to July 1878, without Basilan

keyframe_review.note: 47,924 km2 (no Bulungan area). The state ends on 22 July 1878 (capitulation at Jolo), not 1879, and North Borneo goes to Overbeck and Dent on 22 January 1878 (ledger). Basilan: see the 1752 note.

region.text: Buansa on Jolo island and the Sulu islands

ledger.note: c. 1457: Sharif ul-Hashim founds the Sulu sultanate at Buansa. Infobox 'Established c. 1457' (reign 1457-1480); the article says 'either on 17 November 1405 or 1457'. Bruneian vassal until 1578 (infobox).

region.text: Tawi-Tawi and Basilan, the outer islands of the archipelago

ledger.note: Archipelago grows from Jolo to Tawi-Tawi and Basilan in Cliopatria's 1529 shape. The Sulu page gives only the peak extent ('the islands that bordered the western peninsula of Zamboanga'), no date.

region.text: the north-eastern part of North Borneo 'as a prize for helping the Sultan of Brunei'

ledger.note: 1704: Sulu receives north-eastern Borneo from Brunei. 'The Sultanate of Sulu received the north-eastern part of the territory as a prize for helping the Sultan of Brunei' against his enemies. The Bruneian Civil War of 1660 page (1661-1673) calls the reward a disputed Sulu claim; Cliopatria draws the land from 1673.

region.text: Palawan: 'Sulu gave up Palawan to Spain in 1705'

ledger.note: 1705: Sulu gives up Palawan to Spain.

region.text: Basilan: 'Sulu gave up ... Basilan to Spain in 1762'

ledger.note: 1762: Sulu cedes Basilan to Spain. The Spanish-Moro conflict page instead has 'In 1724, the Jolo sultan made a treaty of peace with the Spaniards, ceding the island of Basilan' and a 'later treaty, dated February 20, 1845, ceded the island of Basilan' (to 'Franco' in its text): the pages disagree on the year.

region.text: Bulungan, after Sulu sacked Berau and Tarakan in 1789

ledger.note: 1789: Bulungan becomes a vassal of Sulu. Infobox 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Sulu (1789-1855)'; 'Sulu sacked both Berau and Tarakan in 1789', after which Bulungan declared independence from Berau. By the early 19th century Sulu was 'the dominant power in northeastern Borneo'.

1855: Bulungan stops paying tribute to Sulu. 'In 1855, Bulungan stopped paying tribute to Sulu for 50 years', making it de facto independent; the page also says Sulu's influence 'officially ended in 1878'.

region.text: Jolo, the town taken by the Spanish expedition of 1876

ledger.note: 1876: Spain takes Jolo. 'An extensive expedition was planned against the Sultan by the captain-general in 1876', the fleet sailing from Manila in February, 'Jolo remaining in undisputed possession of the Spaniards'; the Sulu page: the Spanish captured Jolo in 1876.

region.text: North Borneo, granted to Baron de Overbeck and Alfred Dent by the Sultan of Sulu

ledger.counterpart: British North Borneo Company (Overbeck and Dent)
ledger.note: 22 January 1878: the Sultan of Sulu signs the concession over North Borneo to Overbeck and Dent. The Philippine position is that it 'was only leased'; Malaysia treats it as a cession (the pajakkan dispute). The British North Borneo Company administers it.
July 1878: Spain's occupation of Jolo becomes sovereignty over the archipelago by the 'treaty of the Sultan of Jolo and his datus submitting to Spain, signed at Licup (Jolo) July 22, 1878'.

22 July 1878: the sultan gives up sovereignty to Spain. 'The Sultan of Sulu gave up sovereign rights over his possessions to Spain through the Bases of Peace and Capitulation, signed at Jolo' (North Borneo dispute page; the Spanish-Moro conflict page gives the same date). The sultanate continued nominally to 1915.

wars.name: Spanish-Moro conflict
wars.outcome: Spain landed at Jolo in 1637, sent a punitive expedition in 1731, took Jolo in 1850-1851 and again in 1876; the sultan accepted peace in 1737 and 1836, signed the treaty of 19 April 1851 and the capitulation of 22 July 1878.
wars.note: The infobox dates the conflict 1565-1898. The Sulu page reads the 1851 treaty as one between equals (the sultan's view) or an acceptance of Spanish sovereignty (the Spanish view).

wars.name: Bruneian Civil War of 1660

zones.text: eastern Sabah, the reward Sulu claims for helping Muhyiddin

wars.outcome: Muhyiddin won; Sulu claims eastern Sabah as its reward, a claim the page calls disputed and does not date.
wars.note: Dates 1661-1673 from the body text; the URL says 1660. The Sultan of Sulu is not named.

certainty.note: An island sultanate with a sphere along the Borneo coast; no survey line is dated by the pages opened.
The North Borneo concession (22 January 1878) and the capitulation (22 July 1878) are dated deeds.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Sultanate of Sulu' 1459-1879. Problems found: (1) the 1459 shape is Basilan, not Jolo; (2) there is no shape for 1507-1528; (3) the 1673 shape adds eastern Sabah, which the North Borneo dispute page dates to 1704; (4) the 1748 shape adds exactly the cells of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bulungan (1734-1747), but the Bulungan page makes Bulungan a Sulu vassal only 1789-1855, so the Bulungan land is removed from the direct shapes and carried as vassal_start/vassal_end; (5) Palawan, which the Sulu page says was Sulu's until 1705, is in no Cliopatria shape and is added to the 1673 keyframe; (6) the shapes run to 1879 while the sovereignty ended on 22 July 1878.
Sulu was a vassal of Brunei 1457-1578 (infobox) and a Spanish protectorate 1851-1899 (infobox); those tints belong to the Brunei dossier (sultanate-of-brunei, vassal_start/vassal_end for Sulu) and the Spanish Empire dossier (am-06). Not recorded here because a vassal event sits in the suzerain's ledger.
Disagreements: Basilan cession 1724 (Spanish-Moro page), 1762 (Sulu page), 1845 (a later treaty, 'to Franco' in the Spanish-Moro text); founding 1405 or 1457; the sultanate's end 1878 (capitulation, Cliopatria 1879), 1851 (Spanish protectorate in the infobox) or 1915 (annexation to the United States, 22 March 1915).
The first URL tried, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_claim_to_North_Borneo, did not exist; the North Borneo dispute page replaced it. The Spanish-Moro page was read to character 100000 of 100941.
Counterparts needing dossiers: British North Borneo Company (Overbeck and Dent) from 1878 (a company state of the se-03 or se-04 batch); Kingdom of Bulungan is se-03's.
Gazetteer: 'Buansa' is not a place name in the gazetteer; the capital uses Jolo island coordinates.
